label: David N. Spergel
narrative: Spergel chaired the only formal scientific panel the US government has convened on this subject in the modern era, and the way that panel was constrained is itself evidence. NASA commissioned the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Independent Study Team on 24 May 2022; it began work on 24 October 2022, held a single public meeting on 31 May 2023, and delivered its report on 14 September 2023, the same day it dissolved. Its sixteen members were a genuinely serious cross-section - Federica Bianco, Joshua Semeter, Shelley Wright, Matt Mountain, Walter Scott of Maxar, Reggie Brothers, Mike Gold, Scott Kelly, plus FAA leadership in Warren Randolph and Karlin Toner. The report's conclusions were unremarkable by design: no evidence of extraterrestrial origin, data quality is the binding constraint, NASA should apply rigorous evidence-based methods including AI and crowdsourced observation, and NASA is well placed to lead. What the panel did not have was access to the classified holdings that the entire controversy is about. It was a study of the poverty of the unclassified record, conducted by people barred from the classified one, and NASA then declined at first to name the new director of UAP research it announced the same day. That is the shape of the concealment problem rendered in an organisation chart.
